finding: Training V4 PEF accuracy is higher than overall inference PEF accuracy.
evidence: Training V4 achieved 96.24% accuracy, while overall inference PEF accuracy was 94.17%.
interpretation: V4 improved training fit/fail prediction despite training being more complex.

finding: Training V4 still needs safety margin for deployment safety.
evidence: Without margin, V4 had 8 dangerous failures. At 7.5% margin, dangerous failures dropped to 0.
interpretation: Raw accuracy alone is not enough for safe GPU placement.

finding: The 7.5% training margin trades accuracy for safety.
evidence: Accuracy dropped from 96.24% to 95.11%, but dangerous failures dropped from 8 to 0.
interpretation: This is acceptable when avoiding OOM matters more than maximizing utilization.

evidence: Small reserved-memory errors near memory limits caused dangerous fit/fail mistakes.
interpretation: A numerically accurate estimator can still be unsafe near scheduling boundaries.

finding: Reserved memory is the correct basis for placement simulation.
evidence: PEF simulation used actual and predicted peak reserved memory rather than allocated memory.
interpretation: CUDA allocator reservation determines whether a workload may hit memory-limit boundaries.
